solver_candidate_counterexample: Define h:[0,1]→R by h(0)=0 and h(x)=1 for every x in (0,1]. Then h is differentiable on (0,1) with h'(u)=0≤0 for all u in (0,1), but for any u in (0,1), h(u)=1>0=h(0).
vetter_reason: The lemma is false as stated. The hypothesis only assumes differentiability on the open interval (0,1), so it gives no control over the endpoint value h(0). A function can have h'(u) <= 0 on (0,1) and still satisfy h(u) > h(0) for some u in [0,1), so the claimed conclusion fails.
